Why this requirement?
We deeply appreciate all community contributions - they are essential to Cline's success! To ensure the best use of everyone's time and maintain project direction, we use our Feature Requests discussions board to gauge community interest and validate feature ideas before implementation begins. This helps us focus development efforts on features that will benefit the most users.
-->

### Related Issue

<!-- Replace XXXX with the issue number that this PR addresses -->
**Issue:** #XXXX

### Description

#### What

Make the SDK inference path honor proxy and custom-CA configuration on the
standalone hosts (JetBrains, CLI), and make the standalone proxy dispatcher
install deterministic.

Two commits:

1. **Thread the proxy/CA-aware `fetch` into the SDK inference path.**
   - App (`cline-session-factory.ts`): always build `CoreSessionConfig.providerConfig`
     and carry the proxy/CA-aware `fetch` from `@/shared/net`, not just for cloud
     providers (Bedrock/Vertex).
   - SDK (`handler-factory.ts`): forward `providerConfig.fetch` into `createGateway`
     as both the top-level fallback fetch and the per-provider fetch, so the
     gateway's provider clients actually use it.
   - Adds a unit test asserting the host fetch reaches `createGateway` at both
     levels.
2. **Deterministically install the proxy dispatcher in the standalone core.**
   - `cline-core.ts` now imports `@/shared/net` for its side effect (installing the
     undici `EnvHttpProxyAgent` global dispatcher in the standalone build), first,
     so the install is guaranteed rather than incidental on the import graph.

#### Why

The SDK agent loop never received the host's proxy/CA-aware `fetch`, so inference
through a corporate proxy or to a self-signed / private-CA endpoint failed with
`unable to get local issuer certificate`. In VS Code this `fetch` is the global
fetch (proxy handled by VS Code), so behavior there is unchanged; in the
standalone (JetBrains) build it is undici with `EnvHttpProxyAgent`. Passing
`undefined` is a no-op (the registry resolves
`config?.fetch ?? defaults?.fetch ?? fallbackFetch`), so other SDK consumers are
unaffected.

#### Scope -- what this PR fixes vs. does not

**Fixes:**
- VS Code and JetBrains: the main agent loop now routes inference through the
  proxy/CA-aware fetch.
- JetBrains standalone core: the proxy dispatcher is installed deterministically
  at startup.
- Any SDK host that supplies a `fetch` benefits from the gateway-forwarding
  change.

**Does NOT fix (yet):**
- **The original report is the CLI, and this PR does not resolve it.** The CLI
  builds its session config through a separate path (`apps/cli`) and runs on Bun,
  whose native `fetch` already reads `HTTPS_PROXY` and `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` -- so
  the missing-fetch problem this PR fixes does not exist there. The CLI failure on
  Windows has a different, still-open root cause (Node->Bun runtime change at the
  3.0 rewrite; suspected difference in how Bun-on-Windows reads the Windows system
  trust store / `NODE_USE_SYSTEM_CA`). A **Windows + Bun investigation is in
  progress**, and the CLI fix will land as a **follow-up**.

#### Related

- JetBrains-plugin companion PR (fixes `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` handling on the Kotlin
  side): https://github.com/cline/intellij-plugin/pull/983
- Tracking issue: cline/cline#11175

#### Testing

- `handler-factory` unit test passes (host fetch forwarded top-level + per
  provider).
- `tsc --noEmit` on `apps/vscode` clean for the changed files (pre-existing
  proto-gen errors in `providerCatalogShared.ts` are unrelated and resolve after
  `npm run protos`).
- Reproduced the trust failure + fix end-to-end on macOS against a private-CA
  HTTPS OpenAI-compatible endpoint through the exact `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible`
  client the SDK uses.

#### Notes

- VS Code behavior is unchanged (its `fetch` is the global fetch).
- No new dependencies; no public API changes.

author: santhoshreddylotla
body:
## Summary

This PR fixes the defects found in a full audit of the codebase, focused on the issues that prevent a fresh install from working at all, plus authentication and security bugs.

### Install blockers (fresh install previously could not log in)

- **Seeded admin password hash was invalid** — 62 characters of filler that no password could ever match. Replaced with a real bcrypt hash for `Admin@123` (`database/schema.sql`).
- **seed.sql could not import** — it called PHP functions (`generate_ncr_no()`, `generate_capa_no()`, `generate_quotation_no()`) inside SQL. Replaced with literal document numbers.
- **Missing `cost_center` column** on `fabx_departments` — the Master Setup department create/update wrote to it and failed with a SQL error. Added to the schema.
- **`CREATE DATABASE`/`USE fabx_erp`** statements commented out so imports work on shared hosting where the database has a different name.

### Configuration

- `APP_URL` is now auto-detected from the request (override with `FABX_APP_URL`). Previously it was hardcoded to a Hostinger domain, so every other install redirected users to that remote site.
- DB credentials and the encryption key now read from environment variables (`FABX_DB_*`, `FABX_ENCRYPTION_KEY`) with the previous values as fallbacks, so the existing deployment keeps working.
- `APP_ENV` defaults to `production`; removed the forced `display_errors=1` at the top of `index.php` that exposed stack traces regardless of environment.

### Authentication fixes

- **Account lockout now works**: failed attempts are recorded and the lock is checked *before* password verification. Previously attempts were never incremented and the check ran after verify, so lockout was dead code. New `MAX_FAILED_LOGINS` / `LOCKOUT_MINUTES` constants.
- **Remember-me is now functional**: sessions are restored from the cookie via `attempt_remember_login()` in the router. The cookie stores the raw token; the DB stores its SHA-256 hash. Previously the token was written but never read.
- **Password reset emails are actually sent** (new `send_email()` helper) instead of stashing the token in a demo session variable.
- **Passwords are no longer sanitized** — `strip_tags`/`htmlspecialchars`/`trim` silently corrupted credentials containing special characters. New `input_raw()` helper used for all password fields.
- Session ID regenerated on login/logout (session fixation), logout flash message no longer written to a destroyed session, heartbeat reports real remaining time, and changing your password without entering the current one no longer throws a TypeError.

### Security hardening

- `upload_file()` now verifies MIME type against the claimed extension (CAD formats like dwg/dxf/step/iges are allowed as octet-stream; PHP/HTML/JS content is rejected). The verifier existed before but was never called.
- CSP `font-src` was missing `cdn.jsdelivr.net`, blocking bootstrap-icons fonts.
- Document numbers (`INV-`, `NCR-`, `PO-`…) now use a CSPRNG suffix instead of `uniqid()`, reducing collision risk against UNIQUE columns.
- `paginate()` clamped so empty tables no longer produce page 0 / negative offsets.
- New `notify()` helper to start populating the (previously never-written) notifications table.

## Notes for review

- The audit found further issues not yet addressed in this PR (read-only modules missing write paths, hardcoded dashboard chart data, CSRF on invoice GET actions, the `requireCan('edit')` vs `update` permission mismatch, jQuery loaded from a CSP-blocked origin). Those are planned as follow-up work.
- For existing databases, apply manually: `ALTER TABLE fabx_departments ADD COLUMN cost_center VARCHAR(50) AFTER description;` and update the admin user's password hash if it was seeded with the old value.
- Default login after fresh import: `admin@fabxengineering.com` / `Admin@123` — change it immediately.

---

<!-- kody-pr-summary:start -->
**Risk Summary**
Moderate risk. This pull request introduces caching to the Identity Provider (IDP) resolution path during login. While this improves performance, flawed cache invalidation could result in users seeing stale or incorrect login options. This risk is mitigated by highly targeted invalidation logic and the addition of comprehensive integration tests verifying the caching behavior.

**Functional Purpose and Impact**
This PR implements caching for Identity Providers retrieved during the login flow to optimize performance, particularly in environments utilizing organizations. It ensures that the list of available IDPs is cached efficiently and only invalidated when functionally necessary.

**Key Changes:**
*   **Login IDP Caching**: Implemented Infinispan caching for `getForLogin` operations within `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider`. The cache keys are segmented by the `FetchMode` and the specific organization ID.
*   **Smart Cache Invalidation**: Added precise cache invalidation logic for IDP lifecycle events (create, update, remove). The login caches are **only** invalidated if the affected IDP qualifies for login. For updates, the cache is preserved unless the IDP's login availability status or its organization link changes, preventing unnecessary cache flushes.
*   **Refined Login Predicate**: Updated the `getLoginPredicate` in `IdentityProviderStorageProvider` to correctly evaluate organization-linked IDPs. It now ensures an IDP is only considered for login if it is not linked to an organization or if it is explicitly configured as a public broker.
*   **UI Rendering Safety Check**: Added an explicit `isEnabled()` check in `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean` when filtering IDPs for the login page. This acts as a safeguard to ensure disabled IDPs are not displayed, accounting for scenarios where cached IDP models might be wrapped.
*   **Comprehensive Testing**: Added a detailed integration test (`testCacheIDPForLogin`) to validate cache population, cache hits, and the specific scenarios that should (and should not) trigger cache invalidation.

body:
## Engine Plan E4 — connector trait + registry

Lands `Source`/`Sink` behind a `type`-keyed registry with `file` as the only entry, so later connectors (rest/blob/tcp/grpc/db) are additive — RFC 0003 slice 4.

### What it does
- **`connector.rs`** — async `Source::next()` / `Sink::write()` traits (async because every connector beyond `file` is async I/O; landing the shape now keeps them additive).
- **`registry.rs`** — `type`-keyed dispatch, the one place that knows which connector types exist. Unknown type → clear error.
- **`connectors/file.rs`** — the `file` connector: glob source (sorted = input order, one file → one document) and path sink.
- **Async run loop** — the engine moves onto a tokio runtime. Pipelines are concurrent tasks, connector I/O is async, and the synchronous wasm transform runs in `spawn_blocking`. Connectors are built at startup (before flow modules load), so an unknown type or empty glob aborts the run before any document moves.
- Manifest `Source`/`Sink` structs renamed `SourceSpec`/`SinkSpec`; the file-only check moved from the manifest into the registry.

### Verified (E4 checklist)
- Unknown connector `type` fails with a clear error — registry unit tests + an end-to-end binary test (`unknown source type "rest"`).
- A glob matching three files yields three documents, in input order (artifact test).
- File sink output matches byte-for-byte (artifact test).

27 engine tests pass; `clippy -D warnings` + `fmt` clean.

### Note
tokio's `macros` feature is omitted — the offline crates index lacked `tokio-macros ~2.7.0`. The runtime is built by hand and async test bodies run on a hand-built current-thread runtime, so nothing depends on it.

author: agentydragon
body:
Final increment of cross-module purity. #2088 added the consumption arm; #2094 added the oracle; this PR populates the per-chunk `imported_purities` map in the pipeline.

## What

A program-level pass (`lowering::cross_module`) runs once over the whole artifact before the per-chunk materialization loop:

- **Parses every chunk's entry** — reusing the retained AST where the artifact kept one, re-parsing the chunks stored as raw `Source` (non-selected import targets) so *every* listed chunk participates, not just the selected ones.
- **Resolves each chunk's imports** to their defining chunk via the same `ArtifactIndexes` resolution the specifier rewriter uses, maps each named/default import to `(target chunk, export name)`, and skips namespace imports (member-call sites, not the bare-`Ident` callee the verdict feeds).
- Feeds those `ResolvedImport`s plus each chunk's exports — export aliases **and** `export function`/`export const`/`export class` declarations (which aren't aliases) — to the greatest-fixpoint oracle.

The result is threaded `lowering → materialize → AnalysisHints → build_full`, replacing the empty map at the fact-extraction site. The oracle also gains a skip-unchanged guard in the fixpoint loop, which matters now that it runs over the full chunk set.

Conservative throughout: an unparseable chunk, an import that doesn't resolve into the artifact (vendor packages), or a non-function export yields no verdict and stays `unknown_call`.

## Measured effect (Tana web)

Resolves **631 imported-binding verdicts across 40 route chunks**. The main chunk's factory imports, however, come from the partial-swapped vendor megachunk, whose projected symbols are not local functions in the post-swap body — so the main chunk's atomic-unit conflict is unchanged by this PR. **Making partial-swapped vendor symbols analyzable is the next increment** (it's where React's `memo`/`forwardRef` live).

## Tests

`purity_test` gains a pair: a pure HOF imported from a separate analyzed chunk no longer emits a cross-module S-cycle, while an impure one still does (the oracle propagates real effects, never invents purity). The e2e harness's `with_extra_chunks` wires analyzed-but-not-materialized import targets. All affected e2e suites + `analysis_test` pass.

## Summary

The Ruby SDK's `DataManager` read every config entity through a fictional `["data"]` envelope (`@config["data"]["account_id"]`, `@config["data"]["experiences"]`, …). The live Convert config endpoint emits entities **flat at the root** with no `"data"` wrapper, so in real fetch mode every reader returned `nil`/`[]` while the SDK reported itself ready. The FR65 schema-drift gate in the staging suite caught this on its first scheduled run (2026-06-11), exactly as designed.

This PR adopts **Direction A — flatten Ruby to the flat/root config shape**, matching the JS, PHP, and Android SDKs and the OpenAPI-generated schema. Ruby was the sole outlier.

### Runtime change (single point — `lib/convert_sdk/data_manager.rb`)
- Redefined the private `data` helper to return `@config` (the root snapshot) instead of `@config["data"]`. All eight entity readers route through `data`/`collection`, so this one edit flips them all to root-level reads.
- Tightened `config_available?` from `!@config.nil?` to `!account_id.nil? && !project.nil?` (mirrors JS's `account_id && project.id`), closing the masking hole where an empty/invalid body masqueraded as available.
- `client.rb` and `config.rb` are **byte-unchanged** — both install paths already install the response flat. No public reader method names/signatures changed.

### Test realignment
- Flattened `spec/fixtures/test-config.json` (entities hoisted to root, `"environment"` wrapper dropped — all entity values preserved verbatim).
- Aligned the shared `ConfigFixture` loader, `http_stubs.rb` canned body, and `runtime_recipe_helpers.rb`, plus every consuming spec — driven off the shared loaders to keep duplication low.

## BREAKING CHANGE

The `data:` direct-data option now accepts the **flat** config (entities at root) instead of the `{ "environment", "data" => { … } }` envelope. MAJOR version bump **0.0.0 → 1.0.0** per SemVer (D4). The gem is days-old / unpublished; this ends a divergence rather than introducing one.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 (live fetch mode)** — validated locally against the public key `10035569/10034190`: `config_available? = true`, `account_id = "10035569"`, `project_id = "10034190"`, `experiences = 4`, `features = 6`, `goals = 3`. This is the exact case that returned `nil`/`0` before the fix.
- **AC2 (direct-data flat reads)** — covered by the realigned unit specs.
- **AC3 (staging suite)** — the staging specs were already correct and go green via the runtime fix; **not run in this PR** because no staging credentials (`CONVERT_STAGING_SDK_KEY` / `CONVERT_STAGING_SDK_KEY2` + secret) were present locally, so those groups skip cleanly per qs-04 AC2. They will run on the scheduled `staging.yml` workflow.
- **AC4 (default suite + quality gates)** — green: `rspec` 1125 examples / 0 failures, `rubocop` no offenses, `rbs validate` clean, `steep check` no type errors.
- **AC5 (RBS/Steep)** — signatures and comments updated to the flat shape; type gate green.
- **AC6 (no public API drift)** — `client.rb`/`config.rb` byte-unchanged; `environment_match?` and `?environment=` behavior untouched; all reader signatures preserved.

## Test plan
- [x] `bundle exec rspec` (staging excluded) — 1125 examples, 0 failures
- [x] `bundle exec rubocop` — no offenses
- [x] `bundle exec rbs validate` — clean
- [x] `bundle exec steep check` — no type errors
- [x] Live AC1 smoke (public key `10035569/10034190`) — readers populated, `config_available?` true
- [ ] Staging suite (`--tag staging`) on scheduled run with provisioned credentials (AC3)

author: openningia
body:
Three fixes for the QML sheet, two performance and one UX. Closes #402, closes #419.

  ## 1. Wounds +/- no longer re-projects the whole sheet (#419)

  Clicking the wounds stepper emitted the coarse `character_refreshed`, making every
  PcProxy slice re-emit — the weapons slice alone recomputed every attack/damage roll
  per click. Wounds and health-multiplier changes now go through a narrow
  `wounds_changed` bus signal that only the combat slice listens to. Also drops a
  redundant `notify_character_refreshed()` from the health controller slots (the api
  setters already emit), demotes the per-weapon `calc base atk` log to DEBUG, and
  reads `pcProxy.weapons` once in WeaponsSection.

  ## 2. Memoized PcProxy slice projections 

  Root cause of the "every advancement takes seconds" freeze. QML reads a
  `QVariantList`/`QVariantMap` property through a **live value wrapper**, not a
  detached JS copy: every element access on the QML side (`xs.length`, `xs[i]`,
  `m.key`) re-invokes the Python getter. A section looping over a projection pays
  O(N) getter calls per refresh — SkillsSection alone makes 4N+5 reads per
  `skillsChanged` — and each call rebuilt the projection from the advancement
  history, turning one purchase into an O(N²) walk that grows with the character.

  (The regression surfaced with autosave/resume only because launch now restores the
  real character instead of a blank one — the cost itself predates it.)

  Fix: new `proxies/pc/memo.py` with a `@memoize` decorator stacked under
  `@Property`, serving a per-instance cached projection; `invalidate()` runs right
  before every notify emit, so QML never observes a stale value. Applied to every
  `QVariantList`/`QVariantMap` getter across all 16 slice mixins.

  Measured offscreen on a real character (35 advancements):

  | | before | after |
  |---|---|---|
  | buy skill rank | 1.25–1.48 s | **0.08 s** |
  | engine load | 1.93 s | 0.88 s |

  The two perf fixes are complementary: the narrow signal avoids invalidating slices
  whose data didn't change (and the Repeater teardown that re-emitting causes), the
  memo makes the slices that *are* touched free to re-read.

  **Invariant to preserve:** every emit of a memoized property's notify signal must
  be preceded by `invalidate(self, ...)` in the emitting handler.

  ## 3. Social flag tracks read as rank-tenths (#402)

  Honor/Glory/Status track UX, as suggested in the issue: each dot carries its tenth
  digit (1..9); the wheel wraps the rank at track ends (up from 5.9 → 6.0, down from
  6.0 → 5.9, also on the compact Taint/Infamy tracks); the combined N.N score becomes
  a 20px EB Garamond figure left of the dots. New Theme token `pointDotDigitSize`,
  design system §6.12 updated.

  ## Test plan

  - `python -m unittest discover -s l5r` — 128 tests OK
  - `flake8` (CI selectors) clean
  - Manually exercised advancement purchases, wounds stepper and flag tracks in the
    QML UI with a real character

Closes #402, closes #419, closes #421

We need UPVS URIs to track users' eDesk status. The slovensko-sk container (the UPVS API proxy) didn't expose an identity lookup endpoint, so we built URIs ourselves (from birth number and name) and verified the guesses through batched URI search. The lookup endpoint was added upstream in slovensko-digital/slovensko-sk-api#117, so we can now look URIs up properly and refactor the system around it.

- New `lookupIdentityFO` method on `NasesService` for per-person FO identity lookup against the new endpoint.
- New urgent tier in the UPVS queue: entities with a verified birth number but no URI are resolved via `lookupIdentityFO`, up to 50 per 30s tick, sequentially. Runs first on every tick with its own budget.
- Rate limits are unknown, so an HTTP 429 stops the tick with an alert and the rest is retried next tick (`fromAxiosError` status override keeps the 429 detectable).
- `UpvsQueueService` split by tier into `UrgentLookupService`, `EdeskUriUpdateService`, and `EdeskBatchUpdateService`, plus a queries service deduplicating the backoff SQL. `UpvsQueueService` stays the facade/orchestrator - callers unchanged.
- IAM identity-lookup rejections are saved via a new `IdentityLookupRejection` model/migration. They throw a new `IDENTITY_LOOKUP_REJECTED` error type, and rejected entities are excluded from further processing. A scheduled daily alert reports rejections in the last month.
- Death dates found for Noris-fed external records are logged with their noris ID.
- `createMany` renamed to `getIdentitiesByUris`.
- Scheduler documented in `src/upvs-queue/README.md`

body:
Test PR: feature-authz-crypto-implementation → feature-authz-crypto-baseline

---

<!-- kody-pr-summary:start -->
**Risk Summary:**
Low risk. The changes introduce a specialized, lightweight cryptographic provider for the authorization client and update the provider discovery mechanism to handle multiple providers gracefully using a priority order. Existing providers are given a higher priority than the new one, ensuring backward compatibility and minimizing the impact on existing core server deployments.

**Functional Purpose and Impact:**

*   **Authorization Client Crypto Provider:** Introduced `AuthzClientCryptoProvider`, a new lightweight implementation of `CryptoProvider` specifically designed for the authorization client. It provides essential ECDSA signature format conversions (between concatenated RS and ASN.1 DER) without relying on heavier external libraries.
*   **ASN.1 Encoding/Decoding Utilities:** Added custom `ASN1Encoder` and `ASN1Decoder` utility classes to support the ECDSA signature conversions required by the new authorization client crypto provider.
*   **Provider Priority System:** Modified the `CryptoProvider` interface to include an `order()` method. The `CryptoIntegration` service loader now sorts discovered providers by this order (highest first) and selects the top one, rather than throwing an `IllegalStateException` when multiple providers are present on the classpath. Ignored providers are now logged at the debug level.
*   **Provider Ordering Implementation:** Assigned a priority order of `200` to existing providers (`DefaultCryptoProvider`, `WildFlyElytronProvider`, and `FIPS1402Provider`) and an order of `100` to the new `AuthzClientCryptoProvider`. This ensures full providers take precedence if available.
*   **Automatic Initialization:** Updated the `AuthzClient.create()` method to automatically initialize `CryptoIntegration` using the client's class loader, ensuring cryptographic capabilities are ready when the client is instantiated.
*   **Testing:** Added `ECDSAAlgorithmTest` to validate the correctness of the new ECDSA signature conversion logic across ES256, ES384, and ES512 algorithms.

## What & why

Wraps more of Cinemachine 3.1.4 as declarative YAML behaviours so game authors can reach these camera features without touching C#. Previously only `camera` (output + brain + impulse listener) and `camera follow` were exposed. This adds six more, each as the established 5-file set (Info / Data / `GameBehaviour` / `BehaviourRegistry` / `GameBehaviourFactory`):

| Behaviour | Cinemachine component | Kind |
|---|---|---|
| `camera shake` | `CinemachineImpulseSource` | trigger-fired, any entity |
| `camera noise` | `CinemachineBasicMultiChannelPerlin` | modifier (needs a vcam) |
| `camera zoom` | `CinemachineFollowZoom` | modifier |
| `camera orbit` | `CinemachineOrbitalFollow` vcam | standalone vcam |
| `camera confiner` | `CinemachineConfiner2D/3D` | modifier |
| `camera group` | `CinemachineTargetGroup` + `GroupFraming` | standalone vcam |

## Notes for reviewers

- **Modifier behaviours** (`camera noise`/`zoom`/`confiner`) are pipeline components/extensions that attach to an existing `CinemachineCamera`. They must sit on the same entity as a vcam behaviour and be listed **after** it; a shared `CameraModifier.RequireVirtualCamera` helper throws a clear error otherwise. Documented in each behaviour's `<remarks>`.
- **Noise profiles:** the bundled `NoiseSettings` presets live inside the package and aren't runtime-loadable by name, so a curated subset is copied into `Assets/Behaviours/Camera/Resources/CinemachineNoise/` and loaded via `Resources.Load` (unknown name falls back to `Handheld_normal_mild`). The `.asset` files got fresh Unity-generated GUIDs — no collision with the package copies.
- `camera orbit`/`confiner`/`group` reuse the `CameraTarget`/tag-resolution closure pattern from `camera follow` (re-queried each frame so they catch entities spawned after build). `camera confiner` resolves the bounding collider off the referenced entity lazily until found. Note: the project ships only 3D colliders, so `camera confiner`'s practical path today is `Mode: 3d`.

## Verification

- `check-compile.sh --all` — clean (new files: 0 errors/warnings).
- `run-tests.sh Tests.Behaviours` — **110 passed**, incl. 9 new tests in `CameraBehavioursTests` exercising the real Cinemachine components + the missing-vcam rejection. `Tests.Behaviours.asmdef` now references `Unity.Cinemachine`.
- `generate-docs.sh` — six new sections in `Assets/docs/Behaviours.md`, zero doc-gen warnings naming them.
- `validate-game.sh` — two demo descriptors (`CameraExtrasDemo` 2D, `CameraRigsDemo` 3D) boot cleanly end-to-end.
- `check-format.sh` — correctly formatted.

## Heads-up (pre-existing, not from this PR)

`validate-game` first failed at *instantiate* — but `Asteroids.yaml` fails identically on this master base. It's a pre-existing regression from #266 (optional Position/Rotation): entities omitting `Rotation` hit `NullValueProvider.Get()` in `GameEntityFactory`. The demo descriptors here set explicit zero rotations to sidestep it. Worth a separate fix in `GameEntityFactory` (default Position/Rotation to zero).

body:
## Summary

Fixes a confirmed cross-principal authorization + multi-tenant isolation bug in the MCP front-end.

`requireAuth` authenticated every request only by checking the bearer token resolved to *some* configured client, then passed it to the streamable MCP handler. It never bound an established MCP session to the client that created it. Per-session tool handlers close over the **session creator's** token, so any client holding a valid token that obtained another client's `Mcp-Session-Id` could reuse that session with the creator's identity — tool list, grants, token, and pinned VictoriaLogs tenancy (AccountID).

## Fix

- Authenticate through the SDK's `auth.RequireBearerToken` middleware. Its verifier resolves the token via `Gateway.ResolveClient` and records a `TokenInfo` carrying a stable per-client user id (`sessionUserID`).
- The streamable transport captures that user id at session creation and rejects with **403** any later request on the same session whose user id differs — before any tool handler runs. New sessions still initialize normally.
- The user id is the resolved client identity and is **never empty** (falls back to a token-derived id), so the SDK's hijack guard can never sit inert.
- Static config clients and web-issued tokens (slice-1) bind identically.
- A `normalizeAuth` wrapper preserves `X-API-Key` callers by copying the credential into an `Authorization` header for the middleware.

## Tests (committed, permanent guards)

- `TestSessionBoundToAuthenticatedClient` — client B presenting A's session id to `tools/list` is rejected (403) and does not receive A's tools.
- `TestCrossSessionDispatchDenied` — B cannot dispatch a tool/instance via A's session; the upstream is never reached, so A's pinned AccountID cannot leak.
- `TestStaticAndWebTokensBindToOwnSessions` — both static and web-issued tokens bind to their own sessions and cannot ride each other's.
- `TestSessionUserIDNeverEmpty` — the binding id is never empty (guard never inert).

Verified the tests fail (attack returns 200) when the binding is forced inert, and pass with the fix. `make ci` is green.

> Stacked on PR #5 (base `wall-e/airlock-web-auth-slice-1`) because the fix depends on slice-1's web-issued tokens.

author: virgesmith
body:
Closes #12.

Productionises the `duckdb-spatial` prototype as a reproducible monthly pipeline that builds a single DuckDB database and atomically swaps it into place, so read-only consumers never see a half-built file.

## Pipeline
```
1. extract.to_database       → crime_data table (geometry, BNG)
2. ons_boundaries.load_all   → boundary tables (pfa, lad, msoa, lsoa, oa)
3. transforms.build_all      → H3 count tables + geo lookup tables
4. atomic swap               → <name>.staging.db → <name>.db
```

## Changes
- **`utils.database_path()`** — single source for the DB filename, read from `SAFER_STREETS_DATABASE` in `.env`. Replaces scattered `os.environ["SAFER_STREETS_CRIME_DATABASE"]` lookups, which referenced a var that was never set (would `KeyError`).
- **`extract.to_database`** — new `--db-path` option to redirect output to the staging file without mutating the environment.
- **`ons_boundaries`** — extracted a callable `load_all(db_path, crs="bng", layers=None)` so the orchestrator calls it directly (no subprocess). Module renamed `ons-boundaries.py` → `ons_boundaries.py` to make it importable.
- **`transforms`** (new) — ports the notebook H3 SQL: `crime_counts_h3_{res}`, `h3_{res}_{key}_lookup` views, `h3_{res}_geogs`. Lookups assign each cell to its max-overlap geography (`QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER()`), guaranteeing one row per cell.
- **`build_db`** (new) — `build` command: writes to `<name>.staging.db`, runs all stages, then `os.replace()` promotes it. `build-db` entry point added.

## Testing
- `test_transforms.py`: H3 counts non-zero + NULL coords excluded, all `spatial_id` are valid H3 cell strings, `h3_9_geogs` has no duplicate `spatial_id`.
- Full suite: 147 passed; ruff clean.

## Note
`build`'s `db_path` defaults to `database_path()` (rather than being required as sketched in the issue), so a bare `build-db` works out of the box.

## Interim hold: prevent the Dovecot 2.4 outage recurring tonight

Follow-up to the 2026-06-11 mail outage (PR #59 restored service; lucas42/lucos_mail#60 is the full fix-forward).

### Why
`dependabot-auto-merge.yml` is enabled and the `/postfix` docker updater runs daily at 07:00. Without a hold, Dependabot will **re-open the `alpine:3.21.1 → 3.24.0` bump tomorrow morning and auto-merge it** (CI gates on build, not on a healthy deploy), pulling in Dovecot 2.4 again and re-crash-looping postfix — the same outage, on a timer. The revert in #59 buys less than 24 hours on its own.

### What
Adds an `ignore` for `alpine >= 3.22` to the **`/postfix`** docker updater only. This holds the base at `3.21.x` (so 3.21 **patch** bumps still flow for security currency) while blocking the Dovecot-2.4-bearing 3.22+ line. The `/` and `/docs` updaters are untouched.

### Removal condition
This is explicitly temporary. The inline comment and commit message both point at lucas42/lucos_mail#60 — **remove this ignore entry as part of that PR**, once `dovecot.conf` is migrated to 2.4 and the alpine upgrade can be taken safely.

Note: the docker updater itself remains present, so the `docker-dependabot-updater-present` rollout convention is unaffected.

body:
## Summary

P1 of the reminders redesign: one shared **ScheduleBlock** — the iOS-Reminders-style scheduling UI — composed from the existing pieces (DateField, TimeField, CadenceFrequencySelector, DayChips) plus the two missing controls (hourly interval presets, early-reminder lead-time), wired end-to-end into a single reference modal (**WellnessCheckRoutineModal**).

Two isolated commits, same protected-generator discipline as #49:

### 1. Generator: weekly/biweekly honor multi-day `days[]`
Weekly/biweekly now fire on **every** weekday in a non-empty `days[]` (e.g. "every Wed & Fri"), across all six day-walk paths (feeding/walk/photo/wellness forward + wellness/photo overdue). Biweekly "on" weeks are anchored on the schedule's `startDate`.

**Back-compat is byte-for-byte**: the new path is gated solely on a non-empty `days[]`. Without it, the locked single-`preferredDay` path is untouched (same instances, same date-only ids, same now-anchored biweekly +14). No stored weekly/biweekly item ever persisted a multi-element `days[]` (the modals only wrote `preferredDay`), so existing data is fully covered. Pinned by an id-stability test block.

### 2. Shared ScheduleBlock + wired into WellnessCheckRoutineModal
- Layout: Date → Time → Frequency (full list: Hourly, Daily, Weekly, Biweekly, Monthly, 3/6-Months, Yearly, Custom, Once/Never) → conditional sub-control → Early reminder.
- Conditional controls: Weekly/Biweekly & Custom → multi-select DayChips → `days[]`; Hourly → interval presets → `intervalHours`; Monthly-and-longer / Once → no weekday control (anchored on the picked Date's day-of-month via `startDate`).
- Emits **one canonical object** `{frequency, preferredTime, startDate, preferredDay, days, intervalHours, reminderTiming}` = exactly the generator's per-item read shape. `reminderTiming` is stored-only in P1 (notification layer is P2).
- `wellness_check_schedule` JSONB save/load extended to carry `startDate/days/intervalHours/reminderTiming` (no migration; store passes the array through).
- `CadenceFrequencySelector` gains the full label set + `CADENCE_OPTIONS_FULL` (additive; the 4-item default other modals use is unchanged).

Reference modal confirmed: WELLNESS_CHECK is `CADENCE_SUPPORT = "ALL"` (full forward + overdue), so the dev-guard accepts the whole cadence list and never trips. Rolling ScheduleBlock into the other ~10 modals is **P3, out of scope**.

## Test plan
- **Mobile: 361 → 405** (44 new). Contract test proves the emitted schedule round-trips to ≥1 reminder for **every** cadence with `__DEV__` on (dev-guard never trips); plus pure-mapping tests and a render pin for the conditional controls. Multi-day weekly/biweekly forward/overdue + both biweekly parities + id-stability pinned.
- **Web: 19, untouched.**
- Green under default TZ, **UTC+5:30, and UTC-8**.
- ⚠️ Device pass (pick each cadence → save → reminder in Health → Today) is the manual step before merge.

author: wellington01
body:
Test PR: feature-authz-crypto-implementation-v2 → feature-authz-crypto-baseline

---

<!-- kody-pr-summary:start -->
**Risk Summary:**
Low risk. The changes introduce a priority-based resolution mechanism for cryptographic providers and add a lightweight, standalone crypto provider specifically for the authorization client. The primary risk lies in the modification of the global `CryptoProvider` loading logic, though it is mitigated by assigning higher priorities to the existing default providers.

**Changes and Purpose:**
*   **Introduced Crypto Provider Ordering:** Added an `order()` method to the `CryptoProvider` interface. Updated the `CryptoIntegration` loader to sort discovered providers by this order (highest first) and select the top one, rather than throwing an exception when multiple providers are found on the classpath.
*   **Assigned Priorities to Existing Providers:** Updated `DefaultCryptoProvider`, `WildFlyElytronProvider`, and `FIPS1402Provider` to return a high priority order of `200`.
*   **Added Lightweight Authz Client Crypto Provider:** Created `AuthzClientCryptoProvider` (with a lower priority order of `100`) specifically for the `authz-client`. This allows the authorization client to function and perform necessary cryptographic operations without strictly requiring heavy external crypto dependencies (like BouncyCastle) to be present.
*   **Implemented Standalone ASN.1 Utilities:** Added `ASN1Encoder` and `ASN1Decoder` classes to manually handle the conversion of ECDSA signatures between concatenated RS and ASN.1 DER formats within the new `AuthzClientCryptoProvider`.
*   **Integrated Crypto Initialization:** Updated `AuthzClient.create()` to automatically initialize the `CryptoIntegration` context upon client creation.
*   **Added Testing:** Included `ECDSAAlgorithmTest` to verify the correctness of the new ECDSA signature format conversion logic.

**Functional Impact:**
These changes make the Keycloak Authorization Client more self-sufficient by providing it with a built-in, lightweight mechanism to handle specific cryptographic tasks (like ECDSA signature conversions). The new ordering system ensures that if a full-featured crypto provider (like the Default or FIPS provider) is available in the application environment, it will seamlessly take precedence over the lightweight client provider.
<!-- kody-pr-summary:end -->

author: silranucci
body:
The broadcast challenge requires a mechanism to enable nodes to communicate with each other.

Since Maelstrom relies solely on stdin and stdout streams, and we want to  create a client library in the style of reqwest, a multiplexer is needed  to overcome the single-stream limitation.

This allows us to:
- Instantiate the runtime and the client library independently without requiring them to be created at the same time.
- Abstract all the underlying multiplexing machinery away from the library's public API.
- Evolve both the runtime and the client library independently over time.

author: kemper
body:
## Summary

The three process/tooling asks from the figure round-6 retro (PR #585), making the figure-bake quality gates mechanical instead of eyeballed:

- **Exit-code gates on `scripts/build-catalog-entry.cjs`**: `--max-genus N` fails a bake whose solid's genus exceeds the budget (the headband 2→5 regression class); `--require-labels a,b,c` fails when a listed label is missing, lost, or — when painting — resolves to 0 triangles (the "buried eyes" class that hit two figures last round). Gate failures exit non-zero **before** the entry file is written, so a regressed bake can't be committed by accident. The label inventory is now collected on every bake, painted or not.
- **Durable catalog palettes**: bake palettes used to live only in gitignored `.plans/`, so fresh containers reconstructed them by hand from baked `colorRegions`. They now live committed at `public/catalog/palettes/<id>.json` (13 extracted: the 10 figures + orrery, pocket watch, smiley cactus), regenerated idempotently by the new `scripts/extract-catalog-palettes.cjs`. For entries never committed there, `--palette-from-existing <entry.partwright.json>` derives the palette on the fly. Shared extraction logic lives in `scripts/lib/catalog-palette.cjs`; workflow documented in `public/catalog/README.md`.
- **Pose-recipe regression tests**: the documented recipes in `public/ai/figure.md` are now asserted as rig unit tests — double-biceps (`abduct 95, elbow 95, twist 90` → fists up beside the head), ballet fifth (`abduct 150, elbow 70, twist 90` → hands rounding an "O" above the crown), and a generalized lunge sweep (matched `flex N + knee N` keeps the shin vertical through 85°, the configuration the old cross-product hinge distorted). An FK change that breaks a documented recipe now fails in vitest, not in a sculpt agent's render loop. (Chair-sit was already pinned by the existing sitting-pose test.)

No `src/` changes — scripts, tests, docs, and committed palette data only.

- [x] End-to-end pass-case bake against a live dev server: karate figure with `--palette-from-existing` + `--max-genus 3` + `--require-labels skin,eyes,iris,pupil,headband,belt` → all 11 labels painted, exit 0
